doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Early television: Look Up and Live, What's My Line and Merv Griffin
summary: Heath recalls MJQ appearances on TV shows in the 1950s and says he has tapes, while Holley notes missing TV in the biography.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Right. One more thing, this is another part of the history that’s very murky, your early television appearances. I did some research and I came across a thing in 1955 that the Modern Jazz Quartet appeared on program called “Look Up and Live” on CBS television in 1955.
Was that with the priest [with his collar back]?
Yes! That did happen?
Oh yeah, I got a tape of it!
You do?
Yeah.
We have to talk [laughs].
That was a part of the film presentation, I think.
No, it was not.
No, it was not?
Trust me.
It’s on there. It’s on a tape that I got with, I forget the priest’s name…
Kershaw?
Yeah, he had his collar backwards.
No, that’s never been seen. That tape you have doesn’t hardly exist anymore. You should talk to somebody about that. Now, the other thing I want to talk about…
But we were also on that program with Dorothy Kilgallen, “What’s My Line?”
You were?
Yeah.
What year roughly?
I don’t know. I got it somewhere on tape. “What’s My Line,” and we were on a program with Soupy Sales before Merv Griffin left Philadelphia.
Wow! You were on with Merv Griffin?
It was his show.
I see.
And Soupy Sales was on there too, the comedy and what not. That was in Philadelphia, that was before Merv left Philly.
There was a show called “PM East and PM West?”
Maybe. I don’t remember that one, but I remember… Did you get those listed in the bio?
Yeah, from Lincoln Center.
Oh, no.
In your biography, a lot of your TV stuff is not listed.
The Modern Jazz Quartet, the Biography? You got that? From Evelyn Levin?
Oh, yes, yes. No, a lot of that stuff is not listed.
No kidding.
No, it isn’t. I would’ve remembered that. That’s why I was asking you.
